title: Checkpoint: Africa and the Middle East
objective: After this level you can describe the main landscapes, rivers and resources of Africa and the Middle East.
summary: The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, links the Mediterranean and Red Seas without locks, separates Africa from Asia and lets ships skip the long voyage around Africa.

cards.headline: In 1869, ships got a shortcut that let them skip a whole continent.
cards.body: Before it, a ship sailing between Europe and Asia had to go all the way around Africa. Afterward it could cut through Egypt. The shortcut ties together almost everything in this chapter.

cards.headline: Sea to sea, no locks
cards.body: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea. It needs no locks, because the two seas sit at about the same level. And remember where the Red Sea came from: Level 54's rift, where Arabia pulled away from Africa and the ocean flooded in. Cut across one narrow neck of land, and an ancient crack in the crust becomes a shipping lane.

cards.headline: A line between continents
cards.body: The canal is also a border. It separates Africa from Asia, so Egypt's Sinai Peninsula, east of the canal, lies in Asia. Just west of it spreads the Nile Delta, the silt-built farmland from Level 53. Ships sliding through have Africa on one side and Asia on the other, and they save the whole trip around Africa's Cape of Good Hope.

mascot.line: Left window: Africa. Right window: Asia. Best continental view you can get without leaving your seat.

cards.headline: Chapter 6 complete
learned: The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and Red Seas
It needs no locks: the seas sit at about the same level
Ships skip the long trip around Africa

questions.prompt: Which two seas does the Suez Canal connect?

options.label: The Red Sea and the Dead Sea
options.rationale: The Dead Sea is a landlocked lake.

options.label: The Mediterranean and the Red Sea
The Mediterranean and the Persian Gulf
options.rationale: The Gulf lies on the far side of Arabia.

options.label: The Red Sea and the Arabian Sea
options.rationale: Those meet naturally, with no canal.

questions.explanation: The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, without locks.

questions.prompt: From Level 54: how did the Red Sea, at the canal's southern end, form?

options.label: The Nile carved it on its way to the sea
options.rationale: The Nile flows north to the Mediterranean.

options.label: A glacier scooped it out
Arabia rifted away from Africa and the ocean flooded in
Engineers dug it with the canal
options.rationale: The canal only reaches the Red Sea.

questions.explanation: The Red Sea is a rift between Arabia and Africa that the ocean flooded, which is why a canal could join it to the Mediterranean.

questions.prompt: The Suez Canal divides Africa from Asia. Which side is the Nile Delta on?

options.label: The African side, just west of the canal
The Asian side, in the Sinai
options.rationale: The Sinai lies east of the canal.

options.label: Both sides equally
options.rationale: The delta is west of the canal.

options.label: Neither: it lies far south, in Sudan
options.rationale: The delta is at the mouth, in northern Egypt.

questions.explanation: The Nile Delta lies just west of the canal, in Africa; the Sinai Peninsula to the east is in Asia.

questions.prompt: Rock art of giraffes and hippos in the Sahara shows what?

options.label: Animals were once shipped across it
options.rationale: The rock art shows animals living there.

options.label: It was once green, with lakes and grasslands
Artists invented animals they never saw
options.rationale: They painted animals that lived there.

options.label: It has always been a hot desert
options.rationale: It was green about 11,000 years ago.

questions.explanation: About 11,000 years ago the Sahara was green, with lakes, rivers and grasslands, and people painted the animals they saw.

questions.prompt: Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest point, is one of the volcanoes dotting which feature?

options.label: The Sahara
options.rationale: The Sahara is desert, far to the north.

options.label: The Congo Basin
The Nile Delta
options.rationale: The delta is flat, silt-built land.

options.label: The Great Rift Valley

questions.explanation: Volcanoes, including Kilimanjaro and Mount Kenya, dot the Great Rift Valley.
